culture.title: Tsukkomi
culture.note: Answering a joke with a quick なんでやねん ('why would you!') is the Osaka way to play along.

culture.title: ほんま
culture.note: Kansai for 'really', instead of Tokyo's 本当.

nonverbal.norms: In Osaka, people are more direct and expressive than in Tokyo but still glance away naturally; laughing and reacting out loud (a tsukkomi) matters more than holding a gaze.

fillers.tip: When you need a second to think, say «えーと…» or «あのな…» instead of «um».

tips.formal: In Osaka, staying in です/ます on a date feels distant; drop into casual Kansai speech.
tips.other: «じゃん» and «だよ» sound like Tokyo; in Osaka it's «やん» and «やで».

cultural_moments.milestone: Be the tsukkomi: answer their boke with なんでやねん, or match their banter
cultural_moments.evidence: The learner, in Japanese, answers the date's deliberately silly remark with a tsukkomi-style retort (for example なんでやねん, ちゃうやろ, アホか) or plays along with the joke.
cultural_moments.cue: Say something deliberately absurd about yourself, as a boke, and wait for them to deliver the tsukkomi. One short line.
